en_title: Star Wars: Andor Creator Wants People to 'Blow Up' AI Data Centers by Voting Against Them
cn_title: 《星球大战：安多》主创希望人们投票反对AI数据中心，将其「炸毁」
opus_summary: 《安多》主创托尼·吉尔罗伊对AI生成内容威胁人类制作的电影表示担忧，呼吁影迷投票反对建设更多AI数据中心。他开玩笑说要「炸毁」这些中心，随后澄清指的是在投票箱前反对它们，并表示人们想要人类创作的作品。

paragraphs.en: Star Wars writer Tony Gilroy has sounded the alarm over the rising tide of AI slop that he believes is a threat to human-made movies.
paragraphs.cn: 《星球大战》编剧托尼·吉尔罗伊对越来越多的AI垃圾内容发出警告，他认为这些内容对人类制作的电影构成了威胁。

paragraphs.en: Speaking to Vanity Fair , Gilroy implored movie fans to vote against the spread of AI data centers — and even joking suggested that the artificial intelligence-fuelling tech hubs should be blown up.
paragraphs.cn: 吉尔罗伊在接受Vanity Fair采访时，恳请影迷投票反对AI数据中心的扩张，甚至开玩笑建议炸毁这些为人工智能提供支持的技术中心。

paragraphs.en: Gilroy, who co-wrote Star Wars: Rogue One and created its widely-praised spinoff Andor, was speaking at a panel event to promote his new film Behemoth! , which stars Pedro Pascal as a cellist who records Hollywood film scores and begins having an existential crisis.
paragraphs.cn: 吉尔罗伊参与编写了《侠盗一号：星球大战外传》，并创作了广受好评的衍生剧《安多》。他是在一场宣传新片《Behemoth!》的座谈活动上发表这番言论的。影片由佩德罗·帕斯卡主演，他饰演一名为好莱坞电影配乐录音的大提琴手，开始陷入存在危机。

paragraphs.en: "People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear," Gilroy said regarding the recent surge in AI's capabilities — and the concerns surrounding the technology's cultural, financial, and ecological impact. "I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here [in Los Angeles] is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years... It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans."
paragraphs.cn: 谈及AI能力近期的突飞猛进，以及人们对这项技术在文化、经济和生态方面的影响所抱有的担忧，吉尔罗伊说：「人们对机器人接管的本能抵抗是显而易见的。我不知道会发生什么。我真的不知道。这里［洛杉矶］的音乐界就是这一切的珊瑚礁。过去15年来，它一直在衰亡……现在稍微有了点起色。我认为人们想要的是人类。」

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, Gilmore suggested, the only way that the rampant spread of AI creation will be curbed is via a public pushback to the building of more AI data centers, which are currently needed to fuel the rise in computational power that generative AI must gobble.
paragraphs.cn: Gilmore认为，归根结底，遏制AI创作肆意扩张的唯一方法，是公众抵制建设更多AI数据中心。目前，为了提升生成式AI必须大量消耗的算力，需要这些数据中心提供支持。

paragraphs.en: "Blow up the AI centers, man," Gilmore said, prompting Pascal to joke that Gilmore wasn't actually suggesting citizens should attempt domestic terrorism. "I don't mean to [actually] blow them up," Gilmore clarified. "I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie."
paragraphs.cn: 「把AI中心炸了吧，伙计。」Gilmore说。帕斯卡随即开玩笑说，Gilmore并不是在真的建议公民尝试实施本土恐怖主义活动。「我不是说［真的］把它们炸了，」Gilmore澄清道，「我是说在投票箱前炸掉它们。去投票，把它们炸掉。去看看马斯克的纪录片，伙计。去看看，把四个小时全看完。我是在［这里］推介我的电影，但去看看那部电影。」

paragraphs.en: Here, Gilmore is refering to Musk, the Alex Gibney-directed four-hour unvarnished analysis of the SpaceX and Tesla leader, who also has a stake in AI via X/Twitter and its tool Grok.
paragraphs.cn: Gilmore在这里指的是《Musk》，这是一部由亚历克斯·吉布尼执导、时长四小时的纪录片，对这位SpaceX和Tesla的领导人进行了不加粉饰的剖析。他还通过X/X及其工具Grok涉足AI领域。

paragraphs.en: "I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened," Gilmore concluded. "Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f***ing algorithm, but this movie is organic."
paragraphs.cn: 「我不知道什么会回来，但这是电影中已经出现的、令人难以置信的赋予人性的一面，」Gilmore最后说，「它能被AI取代吗？或许能，而且简单得令人震惊。某个该死的算法上或许有一个情感幅度旋钮，但这部电影是自然形成的。」

paragraphs.en: Last month, OpenAI boss Sam Altman sparked a backlash when he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center. Speaking to YouTuber Cheeky Pint, Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
paragraphs.cn: 上个月，OpenAI老板Sam Altman表示，他认为人们把RAM放在自己的PC里而不是数据中心里「很糟糕」，引发了强烈反对。Altman在与油管主Cheeky Pint交谈时说：「从全球资源分配的角度看，实际上，让每个人都把世界上供应有限的一部分DRAM放在自己的电脑里，而且只有5%的时间在使用，是相当糟糕的。比如说，如果你试图应对这种供应极其受限的环境，就会希望云端的利用率达到最大。而不知为什么，许多人的直觉恰恰与此相反。」

paragraphs.en: The comments were widely ridiculed, with many suggesting that, whether he intended it or not, Altman sounded like he wanted to take away personal ownership of memory and force society to use resources for the benefit of AI companies such as his. Altman later insisted his comments had been taken out of context .
paragraphs.cn: 这番言论遭到广泛嘲讽，许多人认为，无论Altman是否有意，他听起来都像是想剥夺个人对内存的所有权，并迫使社会为了他这样的AI公司的利益使用资源。Altman后来坚称，他的言论被断章取义了。

paragraphs.en: Data centers and the potential impact on jobs and humanity’s very existence from AI are key issues for voters, and are thought to have proven crucial during the recent midterm elections in the U.S. Meanwhile, the AI boom has led to a scarcity of memory to power it, which in turn has caused graphics cards, video game consoles, and PC components to skyrocket in price. Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all raised the prices of their consoles as a result of the ‘RAMpocalypse,’ while the RTX 5080 just disappeared off of Nvidia's marketplace, weeks after the RTX 5090 was all but discontinued.
paragraphs.cn: 数据中心以及AI对就业和人类生存本身的潜在影响，是选民关注的关键问题，并被认为已在近期的美国中期选举中发挥了关键作用。与此同时，AI热潮导致为其提供支持的内存短缺，进而使显卡、电子游戏主机和PC组件的价格飙升。受这场「RAM末日」影响，索尼、微软和任天堂都提高了各自主机的价格；而在RTX 5090几乎停产数周后，RTX 5080也刚刚从Nvidia的商城中消失。
